metadata.title: Combinatorics of Linked Systems of Quartet Trees

nodes.name: Binary Phylogenetic Tree
nodes.statement: A binary phylogenetic tree T=(V,E,phi) on a finite set of taxa X is a triple consisting of vertices V, edges E, and a labeling map phi: X -> L where L is the set of leaves (degree-one vertices), such that (V,E) is an unrooted binary tree and phi is a bijection between X and L.

nodes.name: Isomorphic Phylogenetic Trees
nodes.statement: Phylogenetic trees T1 and T2 on a taxon set X are isomorphic if there exists a bijective map f: V1 -> V2 preserving edges and compatible with the labeling maps, i.e., if {u,v} in E1 then {f(u),f(v)} in E2 and phi2(x) = f(phi1(x)) for all x in X.

nodes.name: Distinguished Edge
nodes.statement: Let T be a binary phylogenetic tree and ab|cd in Q_T. An interior edge e of T is distinguished by ab|cd if e is the only edge that separates a and b from c and d.

nodes.name: Definitive System of Quartet Trees
nodes.statement: A system of quartet trees Q is definitive if, up to isomorphism, there exists a unique binary phylogenetic tree T for which Q is a subset of Q_T.

nodes.name: Bocker's Criterion for Definitiveness
nodes.statement: If T is a binary tree with interior edges labeled E={e1,...,e_{n-3}}, and Q is a system of quartet trees such that each q_i distinguishes a unique edge e_i with |supp(q_i) \ union_{j<i} supp(q_j)| = 1 for i=2,...,n-3, then Q is definitive.
assumptions: T is a binary tree with interior edges labeled E={e1,...,e_{n-3}}
Q is a system of quartet trees where each q_i distinguishes a unique edge e_i in T

nodes.name: Associated Graph G_T(Q)
nodes.statement: For a compatible system of n-3 quartet trees Q on taxon set X, the associated graph G_T(Q) has vertices corresponding to quartet trees that distinguish a unique edge in T, with edges connecting pairs {q_i, q_j} when their distinguished edges are adjacent and |supp({q_i, q_j})| = 5.

nodes.name: Linked System
nodes.statement: Two quartet trees are linked if their vertices are connected in G_T(Q). A system of quartet trees Q is a linked system if G_T(Q) is connected.

nodes.name: Phylogenetically Decisive
nodes.statement: A collection S of four-element subsets of X is phylogenetically decisive if whenever T and T' are binary phylogenetic trees with T|Y = T'|Y for all Y in S, then T = T'.

nodes.name: Linked Systems are Definitive
nodes.statement: Every linked system of quartet trees is definitive.
assumptions: Q is a linked system of quartet trees on a tree T on taxon set X

nodes.name: Proof that Linked Systems are Definitive
nodes.statement: Shows that linked systems have size n-3, each quartet tree distinguishes a unique edge, and because the support of adjacent linked quartet pairs is 5, each additional quartet tree adds exactly one new taxon. Thus the criteria of Bocker's Proposition are met.

nodes.name: Caterpillar Tree
nodes.statement: A caterpillar on n leaves is a binary phylogenetic tree for which there exists an induced subtree on a sequence of distinct interior vertices v_1,...,v_k such that v_i and v_{i+1} are adjacent for all i in {1,...,k-1}.

nodes.name: Lower Bound on k(n)
nodes.statement: The minimal number k(n) such that every collection of quartets S with |S| >= k is decisive satisfies k(n) > C(n,4) - (n-3).
assumptions: S is a collection of quartets on a taxon set [n]

nodes.name: Proof of Lower Bound on k(n)
nodes.statement: Constructs three distinct caterpillar trees T1, T2, T3 differing only in the placement of three taxa {a,b,c} incident to e_1. The complement S' of the n-3 quartets containing all of {a,b,c} has size C(n,4)-(n-3), and T1|Y = T2|Y = T3|Y for all Y in S', showing S' is not decisive.

nodes.name: Quartet Tree Substitution
nodes.statement: Let q=ij|kh distinguish edge e with taxa partitioned into sets A_i, A_j, A_k, A_h. For x in X - supp(q), the quartet tree substitution q(x) is the unique quartet tree in which x replaces the taxon in supp(q) that belongs to the same partition set A_n as x.

nodes.name: Vine of a Quartet Tree
nodes.statement: Let quartet tree q distinguish an edge e of a tree. The vine of q is v(q) = {q} union {q(x) : x in X - supp(q)}. The quartet tree q is called the seed of the vine.

nodes.name: Linked Vines
nodes.statement: Two vines v(q_i) and v(q_j) are linked if for each q_i in v(q_i) there exists a unique q_j in v(q_j) such that q_i and q_j are linked.

nodes.name: Linked Quartet Trees Produce Linked Vines
nodes.statement: If q_i and q_j are linked quartet trees, then the associated vines v(q_i) and v(q_j) are linked.
assumptions: q_i and q_j are linked quartet trees distinguishing adjacent edges e_i and e_j
conclusions: The vines v(q_i) and v(q_j) are linked

nodes.name: Proof that Linked Quartets Produce Linked Vines
nodes.statement: Uses quartet tree substitution on both q_i and q_j with each taxon x. Shows by case analysis that |supp(q_i(x), q_j(x))| cannot be 4 (would imply same edge) or 6 (would require x in two partition sets), so it must be 5, establishing the linking condition.

nodes.name: Meshed System
nodes.statement: A meshed system on a tree T with taxon set X is an (n-3) by (n-3) array of quartet trees, where each row is a linked system and each column is a vine.

nodes.name: Existence of Meshed Systems
nodes.statement: For any binary phylogenetic tree T on a taxon set X, the system Q_T of all quartet trees displayed by T contains a meshed system.
assumptions: T is a binary phylogenetic tree on a taxon set X
conclusions: Q_T contains a meshed system (an (n-3) x (n-3) array where rows are linked systems and columns are vines)

nodes.name: Proof of Existence of Meshed Systems
nodes.statement: Labels interior edges starting from one adjacent to a cherry. Constructs a linked system for the first row by choosing quartet trees that distinguish adjacent edges with support overlap 5. Then extends each quartet tree into a vine via substitution. By the linked vines theorem, the resulting rows are all linked systems.

nodes.name: Minimal k(n) for Decisiveness
nodes.statement: The number k(n) = C(n,4) - (n-4) is the smallest number such that every collection of quartets S on taxon set [n] with |S| >= k is decisive.
assumptions: S is a collection of quartets on a taxon set X = [n]
conclusions: k(n) = C(n,4) - (n-4) is the minimal such threshold

nodes.name: Proof of Minimal k(n)
nodes.statement: By the meshed system theorem, Q_T contains n-3 disjoint linked systems. If |Q| >= C(n,4) - (n-4), then by the pigeonhole principle Q must contain at least one complete linked system. By the linked-definitive theorem, Q is definitive, so T is the unique tree displaying Q, establishing decisiveness. The lower bound from the caterpillar construction shows this is tight.

nodes.name: Lower Bound on Probability of Decisiveness
nodes.statement: The probability p(X,k) that an arbitrary collection of k quartets is decisive satisfies p(X,k) >= sum_{i=1}^{n-3} (-1)^{i+1} C(n-3,i) C(|Q_T|-i(n-3), |Q_T|-k) / C(|Q_T|, k).
assumptions: S is a collection of k quartets from a taxon set X

nodes.name: Proof of Probability Lower Bound
nodes.statement: If Q contains a definitive set then S is decisive. By the linked-definitive theorem, containing a linked system suffices. The probability is bounded below by the probability that Q contains at least one of the n-3 disjoint linked systems from the meshed system. The formula follows from the inclusion-exclusion principle applied to counting subsets of size k containing at least one disjoint linked system.
